findings.title: Commit steps are checkbox tasks, not plain `**Commit**:` markers
findings.description:
Tasks 2C, 3C, 4C, 5C and 6C (lines 71, 94, 117, 126, 134) are written as `- [ ] **Task NC: Commit** — …` checklist items. A commit checkbox can only be ticked after the commit it describes, which leaves either a dirty tree or a follow-up commit that only checks a box. Task 6's own success line ("working tree clean after commit", line 132) cannot hold once 6C is ticked.

Fix: replace each with a plain line, for example `**Commit**: feat(core): add slice design heading validator`, at the same five positions. The placement itself is right: each sits after an implementation and test pair, at a working, tested point.

findings.title: Task 4T's setup pointer conflicts with its real-design tests
findings.description:
Line 107 says to follow the setup in `validate.test.ts`. That file mocks the core validator and uses a fake project root (`projectPath: '/tmp/test'`, `packages/cli/tests/commands/validate.test.ts:18-29`). The real-design bullet on line 108 needs the opposite: the real core function, and a project whose resolved root is the repo root so the real template is found. A junior implementer following line 107 either mocks core, which makes the test meaningless against the slice's "command test running real slice designs" requirement, or gets exit 2 for a missing template under `/tmp/test`.

Two fixes, both one line each:
- **Setup:** point the whole file at the `validate-worktree-scope.test.ts` pattern (real core, only `FileProjectStore` mocked), and state that the mocked project's `projectPath` is the repo root for the real-design cases. Line 114 already cites that file, but only for the worktree bullet.
- **File selection:** line 108 says "several files … that pass the bash script today" without saying how to pick them. Add a step: run `project-documents/ai-project-guide/scripts/validate-slice-design` over `project-documents/user/slices/*-slice.*.md`, pick a few that print `PASS`, and hard-code those names. Otherwise a wrong pick fails the test before Task 5's sweep exists to explain it, and the implementer may loosen the validator to make it pass.

findings.title: Task 5C's commit message does not fit a code fix
findings.description: Task 5 says an unexplained `DIFF` is a bug to fix with an added test, but the only commit message offered is `docs: record slice 214 parity sweep results`. Add a second message for the fix case, such as `fix(core): …`, or say the type follows what changed.

findings.title: No test covers an unreadable file or unreadable template
findings.description: Task 3 implements the readable check, and Task 3T covers missing file, directory, missing template and no-marker template, but nothing exercises the unreadable case. The slice mandates only the valid-before-missing test, and permission tests are unreliable when CI runs as root, so this is acceptable as written.
